messages.content: Hello Clara,! I'd love to get to know you a little before your stay at Seven Secrets by Hanging Gardens, so the team can think about the details that matter to you. This chat is optional; you can skip a question or finish whenever you like. What brings you here this time?
My husband Marc, our seven-year-old son Leo and I are coming for our tenth wedding anniversary.
A tenth anniversary with Leo along sounds like a lovely family milestone. Have you started imagining how you’d like to mark it here—something all three of you can enjoy, or a moment for you and Marc?
We'd like family time and one romantic dinner just the two of us, perhaps on the beach. Nothing booked yet; we'd need to work around Leo.

That sounds like a lovely balance of family time and a moment for you and Marc. How are you picturing Leo fitting into the dinner evening—would you like him included for part of it, or do you have another arrangement in mind?
We'd be happy with a trusted sitter who can keep him busy for a couple of hours, so Marc and I can have that evening together.

A couple of hours together could make a lovely anniversary pause. I can’t assume childcare is available here, so the team would need to check; meanwhile, what kind of food would you and Marc most enjoy for that dinner?
Local food would be lovely. I'm also keen to learn some local cooking; Marc is happy to try things. We don't have any dietary restrictions ourselves.

Local food and a chance to learn some cooking could make a lovely thread through the stay. Are there particular Indonesian dishes or flavours you and Marc are especially keen to taste or learn to make—and what might Leo enjoy?
I don't know the dish names yet—we'd enjoy learning. Leo isn't fussy, but he has a severe shellfish allergy and we carry an EpiPen.

Thank you for flagging Leo’s severe shellfish allergy and that you carry an EpiPen; the hotel team would need to confirm food handling directly. To help shape the everyday side of the stay, what do you and Marc usually enjoy for breakfast or to drink, and is there anything Leo particularly likes?
We like taking breakfast slowly—fruit and eggs. I love coconut water, Marc likes fresh pineapple juice, and Leo would always choose watermelon juice.
A slow breakfast with those individual juices sounds like a lovely start to the day. What little snack or treat would each of you enjoy later on—sweet or savoury?
Marc and I love mango, coconut and pineapple. Leo is more of a chocolate-chip-cookie boy, though he loves watermelon too.

Mango, coconut and pineapple for you and Marc, and a chocolate-chip cookie for Leo—those are useful little details. When you’re away, is there anything that helps each of you sleep comfortably, or something from home you’d especially appreciate having in the room?
About 24 degrees works for us. I like a firm pillow, Marc a soft one; Leo isn't bothered. Marc's a light sleeper. We share a duvet, and Leo has his own blanket.

That gives a helpful picture of how you each sleep, especially with Marc being a light sleeper. Is there anything in particular that helps him sleep well away from home, or something any of you would especially appreciate having in the room?
Just somewhere quiet for Marc. Nothing else in particular—we're quite easy.
A quiet place for Marc to sleep sounds important. For your anniversary, would a small personal touch feel welcome—and are there any flowers or scents you especially like or would rather avoid?
Yes, a quiet little anniversary touch would be nice. I love frangipani and light natural coconut scents, not heavy artificial perfumes. Marc sneezes around heavy pollen.

Frangipani and a light, natural coconut scent—rather than heavy perfume—are useful distinctions, especially with Marc’s sneezing around heavy pollen. Is there a small sentiment, shared memory or private joke that would make an anniversary touch feel personal to you, or would you rather keep it simple?
I'd love a note on Marc's pillow saying: « Ten years, and I would choose you again. Thank you for being my adventure. » Just something private, no loud public celebration.

That line is quietly lovely, and the private tone is clear. What does Leo most enjoy doing or playing, so the family time—and any sitter arrangement the team may be able to explore—can feel right for him?
Leo is fascinated by turtles and sea life. He'd love seeing them, and stories or games about the ocean would keep him happy.

Turtles and sea-life stories sound like a lovely thread for Leo. For seeing marine life, would a short boat outing feel right for your family, if a suitable option is available, or would you prefer to keep things shore-based?
A boat outing and island hopping together would be great. Marc is also keen on snorkelling or diving, so he'd be happy to do that separately one morning.

A family boat outing and a separate morning on the water for Marc both sound like good possibilities to explore with the team. For the island-hopping day, would you all want time to swim or snorkel, or is seeing turtles and exploring from the boat more your speed?
A gentle mix of seeing marine life, exploring and a swim would suit us. We don't have anything more specific in mind.

A gentle mix of marine life, exploring and a swim sounds like a lovely pace; the team can check what suitable options are available. Since you enjoy slow breakfasts, do either you or Marc have a usual coffee or tea order, or another morning ritual you like to keep?
The juices I mentioned are our favourites; no special coffee or tea order. Marc likes a morning swim, and I'm happy with a book by the pool.

A slow breakfast followed by Marc’s swim and your book by the pool sounds like a lovely rhythm. When you’re at the resort, do you enjoy staff offering suggestions and checking in, or would you rather seek them out when you need something?
We enjoy a warm, chatty team and suggestions along the way. We're happy to get to know people while we're there.
It’s lovely that you enjoy getting to know the team along the way. For the anniversary evening, what time of day would make a couple of hours together easiest around Leo?
One evening, but we're flexible about the time. Nothing else is fixed yet.

A flexible evening leaves room to make the anniversary dinner fit naturally around Leo. You mentioned wanting to learn local cooking—would you most enjoy getting hands-on with preparing a dish, or discovering local food through tasting and explanation?
Hands-on cooking would be lovely. I'd enjoy learning to make a local dish.
Hands-on sounds like a lovely way to get to know local cooking. Would you picture it as something the three of you could enjoy together, or more as time for you and Marc?
I'd enjoy that myself. No need to make it a family activity.

So the cooking would be a little experience for you, rather than a family activity. If the team can explore a hands-on option, would you prefer a one-to-one lesson or would you be happy to join a small group?
Either would be fine. I don't have a preference.

Either format works for the cooking experience, so there’s no need to tailor it that way. Apart from the family boat outing and Marc’s separate morning on the water, do you have any fixed commitments, or would you prefer to keep most of the stay open?
No fixed commitments—we'd like to keep the stay open. I think that covers everything for us, thank you.

Thank you, Clara. You’ve given us a lovely picture of the family time, your anniversary, and the little things that would make the stay feel like yours; I hope you all have a wonderful time at Seven Secrets.

# Seven Secrets by Hanging Gardens, Lombok — service DNA

## 1. Review status and use

Research checked: 5 October 2026. Public preparation; operator review pending; no operational hotel confirmation. Official pages, dated reporting and the local pre-visit profile have different evidence strength. Historical prices are isolated below. Composition examples are proposals, not an exhaustive catalogue.

Historical reference: references/knowledge/seven_secrets_capability_profile.txt, a preparation profile before a visit, including an April 2026 form observation. It remains an audit reference, not the current authoritative description.

## 2. Identity and service interpretation

A beachfront Lombok resort with spacious suites, contemporary art/design, food, spa and activity coordination. The official site supports both private accommodation and shared beach/pool spaces. [V01–V05]

An April 2025 first-hand report describes 24 suites, a DJ booth/beach-club atmosphere and seasonal or private use of Majesty. It is dated external observation, not a current entertainment programme or operating policy. [V14]

Interpretation: do not inherit the historical profile's narrow assumption that only quiet couples fit. Privacy, social energy, food and activity may coexist. Ask which balance the guest wants and confirm the actual programme. Do not classify sports, families or small professional gatherings as inherently incompatible without an explicit constraint.

## 3. Spaces, teams and working capabilities

| Resource | Published capability | Boundary / owner |
|---|---|---|
| L'Angelo Bianco | Breakfast/lunch/dinner; seafood, Indonesian and international cooking | F&B; live menu and kitchen hours [V05] |
| Majesty / pool bar | Wine/dining setting and poolside drinks/tapas | F&B; actual opening/booking status to confirm [V05, V14] |
| Flexible dining locations | Dining can be arranged in room, terrace, beach or pool settings | F&B/guest services: time, weather, safety, privacy, setup charge and staffing [V05] |
| Spa | Treatments, flower bath and resident child treatment | Spa: suitability, age rules, slot and prices [V06] |
| Activity coordination | Catamaran arrangements, diving, helicopter and golf coordination | Guest services/activity team; availability, operator and weather [V08] |

The scope of any concierge/butler role and named operational owner still needs direct confirmation. Historical review names are not a current staff roster. Do not contact suppliers or create bookings through this DNA.

## 4. Rooms, sleep and practical comfort

| Category | Published size/resources | Preparation implications |
|---|---|---|
| Garden View Suite | 98 m², sofa bed, jacuzzi, minibar/wine storage, daybed, semi-outdoor shower | Check occupancy, actual bedding and privacy [V02] |
| Ocean View Suite | 98 m², similar listed resources with ocean outlook | View does not prove noise level or weather protection [V03] |
| Mountain View Suite | 80 m², jacuzzi and suite amenities | Distinct category; no automatic couple/family assignment [V04] |

Room pages advertise 24-hour room service; the dining page gives 07:00–21:00. This may distinguish service availability from full kitchen hours, but it has not been resolved. Ask about the actual late menu. Private jacuzzi does not establish room preparation permission, temperature customisation or an included flower bath. [V02–V05]

A pillow menu, room-aroma choice, fruit/welcome amenities and afternoon tea appear in a reseller listing. Pillow choice is also reported by an OTA. These are leads, not primary-confirmed inclusions; exact pillow types, pricing and current entitlement remain unknown. No firmness menu is invented. [V15, V16]

## 5. Food and drink resources

The official dining page establishes Indonesian/international cuisine, seafood, wine, cocktails and location flexibility. No reliable current full food, cocktail, breakfast or allergen price menu was found through the official site and targeted document searches. Do not replace that gap with a generic tropical-fruit inventory. [V05]

The dated independent report names Laksa Bogor, Octopus Taliwang and Sate Rembiga, reports vegetarian/vegan breakfast choices and a welcome-drink choice. These show historical culinary direction only; recipes, ingredients, stock, present menu and prices require confirmation. [V14]

The spa page mentions roselle tea before and ginger tea after one treatment, plus fresh avocado/aloe in a wrap. This establishes spa use at the time of publication, not food-grade stock at the bar or permission to move spa ingredients into drinks. The tea practice is a useful lead for an alcohol-free welcome preference, subject to spa/F&B coordination. [V06]

The historical pre-arrival form's vegetarian, vegan or gluten-free options show that such requests were collected. They do not certify recipes, cross-contact controls or every requested substitution. Obtain the actual menus and allergy process before turning dietary requests into execution instructions.

## 6. Wellness, activities and family resources

Spa hours are published as 10:00–22:00; advance reservation is requested. The page lists a 90-minute facial, an avocado/aloe wrap and an aromatic flower/oil bath; standalone prices are not published in the reviewed material. Product branding on the page should be rechecked before naming a current brand to a guest. [V06]

The child treatment is 45 minutes for ages 6–13, residents only, with an adult present for under-10s. This does not establish a kids' club or babysitter. Fitness is published 07:00–22:00 and for ages 16+. [V06, V07]

Activities page describes tailored catamaran routes/duration/vessels, diving with a claimed PADI centre, helicopter arrangements and golf coordination. The website's reef-distance claim is not a safety assessment. Ask staff about current certified operator, age/ability requirements, sea conditions, transfers, equipment and cancellation. No current activity tariff was verified. [V08]

## 7. Packages, extras and price conditions

| Public arrangement | Building blocks | Price and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Three-night honeymoon | Suite, one floating breakfast, honeymoon setup/gift, private dinner/champagne, one 90-minute couple massage, first-night sunset cocktails | Quote; “Secret Panoramic” category does not map clearly to current room names [V09] |
| Six-night honeymoon | Longer stay, two floating breakfasts and two couple massages among inclusions | Quote; “Secret Deluxe” mapping and full terms to confirm [V09] |
| Hanging Gardens Bali + Seven Secrets | Four nights, two at each; breakfasts and specified transfers/activities | From IDR 44,171,000 for two, including 21% service/government tax; inter-island transport not assumed included [V10] |
| Same two properties, six nights | Three nights each; adds 60-minute couple massage at each property | From IDR 66,990,450 for two, 21% included [V10] |
| Nandini + Seven Secrets | Separate four-night two-property offer | From IDR 23,190,600 for two, 21% included; different Bali property/rooms [V11] |
| Nandini + Seven Secrets, six nights | Longer version with massage | From IDR 34,385,900 for two, 21% included [V11] |

These are starting prices for named packages, not standalone room/service prices or date-specific quotes. Offer pages have no sufficient live availability confirmation. “Endless Shores” and “Luxe Lombok Escape” appear on the offers index without a verified fixed price/discount used here. [V12]

Historical only — local profile records an April 2026 form showing airport transfer IDR 650,000; harbour transfer IDR 250,000; a Gili half-day for two IDR 2,000,000++; two-person arrangements at IDR 4,000,000++ and IDR 6,000,000++. These have not been corroborated as current. Vehicle/route, inclusions, taxes and validity are incomplete. Do not quote or calculate from them.

## 8. Composition possibilities — proposals for staff

| Volunteered guest cue | Known resources | Possible composition | Owner and checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wants a quiet first evening after travel | Suite, flexible dining location, Indonesian kitchen [V02–V05] | Simple dinner at an appropriate private setting, with an agreed arrival pace | Guest services + F&B: kitchen hours, menu, weather, setup, fee and noise; not automatic private beach dining |
| Likes ginger and avoids alcohol | Spa ginger/roselle tea practice plus bar [V05, V06] | Ask whether F&B can offer an appropriate tea-based arrival drink | F&B + spa: food-grade ingredients, service location, recipe, caffeine/sweetness and charge; no assumed shared stock |
| Anniversary without champagne or decoration | Honeymoon coordination, private dinner, massage [V09] | Explore replacing unwanted ceremonial elements with a quieter food/wellness sequence | Guest services: package eligibility, substitution authority, budget and availability; no assumed discount |
| Wants marine discovery but tires easily | Tailored catamaran/dive coordination [V08] | Ask activity team about a shorter, suitable sea outing | Team: conditions, operator, accessibility, ability, equipment, transfer, price and cancellation; no guaranteed calm water |
| Family wants one suitable spa moment | Published child treatment [V06] | Age-appropriate treatment at a practical time | Spa: actual age, supervision, suitability, appointment and fee; no wider childcare promise |
| Likes privacy but also some social atmosphere | Suite privacy, shared pool/beach venues [V02–V05, V14] | Let staff propose a balance of private and social moments | Guest services: live programme and noise, venue hours and guest preference; dated DJ reporting is not a current schedule |

These are starting points for composition. Staff may adapt other combinations of known spaces and expertise, provided the brief names the assumptions and checks.

## 9. Conversation and brief handoff

Use the guest's purpose, desired privacy/social balance, food preferences and appetite for activity. Don't lead with honeymoon packages or ask a long activity checklist. Collect relevant swim/boat comfort as a preference, not medical profiling. Experiences go to confirmed concierge or reception/guest services; room requests to housekeeping; food to F&B; treatments and water activity suitability to professionals. No proposals after personalisation refusal.

## 10. Review queue and evidence conflicts

Most valuable missing documents: current restaurant/breakfast/bar menus with prices; spa tariff; pillow/linen menu; pre-arrival form and transfer/activity tariffs; room occupancy/accessibility; allergy procedures; adaptation budgets and responsible teams.

Resolve room names in honeymoon offers, 24-hour room service versus 07:00–21:00 dining, current Majesty opening and seasonal programme. Keep Hanging Gardens Bali and Nandini offers separate. Historical exclusions on sports/events and dated guest-review staff names are not current operational constraints. Secondary pillow/amenity claims require primary confirmation. No hotel contact or booking check was made.

## 11. Source register

All checked on 2026-10-05. “Reported” entries are external sources and must not be treated as property confirmation.

A) BASIC INFO

Clara, her husband Marc and their seven-year-old son Leo; 15–20 May 2027, party of three. Family stay marking Clara and Marc’s tenth wedding anniversary. They want family time and one private dinner for two, working around Leo. Nothing is booked; they have no fixed commitments and want to keep the stay open.

B) COORDINATION

Reception is the handoff lead. Hotel information is public-source preparation only; operational review is pending, so no service, availability, booking or price is confirmed. Reception should confirm the responsible experience contact and coordinate the relevant checks with housekeeping, F&B and activity staff.

Critical cross-team food alert: Leo has a severe shellfish allergy and the family carries an EpiPen. Before offering or serving food or drink for him, kitchen and any other relevant service staff must confirm ingredients and cross-contact controls under the hotel’s actual protocols. Do not describe any item as safe without that confirmation.

C) GUEST PROFILE

Clara is interested in local food and would enjoy learning to cook a local dish hands-on herself; Marc is happy to try local food. They have no dietary restrictions themselves and do not yet have particular dish names in mind.

Leo is fascinated by turtles and sea life; ocean stories or games would keep him happy. The family would enjoy a boat outing and island hopping with a gentle mix of marine-life viewing, exploring and swimming. Marc is also interested in a separate morning snorkelling or diving outing.
